p1.title: "Failed consume/alias retains the old owner and lock" is unachievable after live consumption begins; the predecessor and the shared transport are already gone
p1.evidence: plan docs/production-hardening/production-hardening-tdd-plan-v2.md:94169-94172 and :94224-94226 promise that any failed consume/alias retains the old owner and lock and that GREEN proves "failed replacement retention". In the real owner, consumeCreatorSuccessorLive -> activateV3LivePlane retires the predecessor first: packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:7114 computes reusesTransport for the same stable topic, :7261 sets existing.active = false and :7266 installs the successor as the topic owner — all before packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:7383 material.terminalizeSource(). On the two post-consumption failure paths (v3-live.ts:7384 terminalize-failure, and packages/node/src/creator-adoption-activate.ts:220-227 alias-failure) rawHandle.deactivate() runs deactivateRegistration (v3-live.ts:3465-3486), which unsubscribes the shared stable topic (:3475) and closes the shared queue (:3480). The retained predecessor wrapper then wraps a registration with active === false, so its own deactivate is a no-op (v3-live.ts:7049-7051): the room would hold a lock and a map entry over a plane that can neither ingest nor publish, while the close handle has already moved to "successor-adopted" (packages/node/src/creator-close.ts:638-643).
p1.required_fix: Restate retention as stable-topic entry plus lock custody only, and pin the boundary: every genuinely reversible refusal must occur strictly before consumeCreatorSuccessorLive; after it returns, the predecessor is retired and terminal and (on failure) the shared topic/queue are torn down. Require the failed-live-consumption and failed-alias/cleanup mutants to assert those observed facts (predecessor registration inactive, topic unsubscribed, queue closed, close handle terminal) and to surface an explicit unavailable/stalled room state with an exact code, rather than asserting a usable retained predecessor.

p1.title: Duplicate-adoption no-op predicate is under-specified in a way that would refuse the legitimate epoch 1 -> 2 adoption
p1.evidence: plan :94198-94201 replaces the latch with "once the current authority already equals the durable authenticated head, an additional call is an idempotent no-op". In the room, the floor's stable head only advances inside the adoption itself (examples/v3-room/src/index.ts:3524-3534 beginRoomHeadAdvance -> publish -> commitRoomHeadAdvance) and the authority is only set at :3586. Immediately after a genuine sealEpoch() at epoch 1 the authority is epoch 1 and openedRoomHeadState.stable is still epoch 1, so a floor/authority equality reading no-ops exactly the adoption this slice must enable; the alternative reading (compare against the live plane's current ephemeral authority) never no-ops. The current latch it replaces is examples/v3-room/src/index.ts:3502.
p1.required_fix: Name the exact authenticated predicate and its evaluation point — e.g. no-op only when the currently bound close handle reports status().lifecycle !== "successor-pending-adoption" (packages/node/src/creator-close.ts:666-684) and the authority/floor already equal the active plane's authenticated currentEphemeralAuthority tuple — and add a GREEN case proving that a fresh seal at epoch 1 admits adoption while the floor stable is still 1, and that a duplicate call with no pending successor no-ops instead of throwing sealed-live-unavailable.

p1.title: Compatibility boundary omits the two retained epoch-1 authority oracles the epoch-2 assertions must not silently relax
p1.evidence: plan :94086-94097 declares the boundary "exact" and names only the tests-only CreatorLiveCloseResult declaration in packages/storage-browser/tests/phase-5e-creator-live-close.pw.ts. Two retained Phase-6a owners hard-pin epoch 1 and are consumed by gates this slice must keep: tests/fixtures/phase-6a-v3/creator-successor-product-contract.ts:574 (record.epoch === 1 inside isD108d2Authority), used by the retained assertion at packages/storage-browser/tests/phase-6a-creator-successor-product.pw.ts:740; and the harness's independent raw-authority derivation at packages/storage-browser/tests/assets/phase-6a-creator-successor-product-entry.ts:682 (selects only the trust record with currentEpoch === 1) and :702 (emits literal epoch: 1), consumed by exportSuccessor/carrier.authority at :735-742 of the same test. An epoch-2 authority assertion has no producer today, so the cheapest path is to loosen both to a numeric check, which silently weakens the retained D.108d2 oracle equality.
p1.required_fix: Name both owners in the compatibility section; require isD108d2Authority's epoch === 1 pin and the retained D.108d2 oracle comparison to stay byte-exact; add a separate epoch-parameterized predicate and raw-authority derivation used only by the new D.110c-b title, and forbid replacing either epoch pin with a typeof/number check.

p2.title: Deferred cold-reopen literal creator-adoption.ts:1030 is missing from the debt enumeration
p2.evidence: plan :94244-94247 lists cold-reopen literals at creator-adoption.ts:840,943-944,1052,1229-1230 but omits packages/node/src/creator-adoption.ts:1030 (successorProjection.record.epoch !== 1), which sits in the same reopenCreatorSuccessorMaterial function and is the only remaining hot-emitted-value dependency there once Batch 1 emits the authenticated successor epoch at :545/:565.
p2.disposition: Add :1030 to the D.110c-0b1/D.110c-c debt list and add one Batch-1 GREEN assertion that reopenCreatorSuccessorAdoption of an epoch>=2 successor still fails closed with the existing chain-invalid classification rather than activating.

p2.title: Batch-1 Node gate requires "one browser lock", which the Node realm cannot produce
p2.evidence: plan :94176-94177 requires the focused Node test to prove "one active topic owner and one browser lock". packages/node/src/creator-adoption-activate.ts:106-114 browserLockRealm() requires window === globalThis or an object globalThis.location; the root suite runs in the default node environment (vite.config.mts:86-108 sets no test.environment), so acquireBrowserLock returns undefined and no lock exists. Satisfying the clause in Node would require synthesizing location/navigator.locks, i.e. a fake lock manager.
p2.disposition: Move the lock-custody clause to the Chromium Batch-2 gate (which already requires "exactly one active owner/lock") and restate the Node gate as one active topic owner with the no-lock realm path exercised and no synthetic LockManager installed.

p2.title: The new Chromium title's "independent genuine room" has no pinned realm, database, or channel in a serial retained file
p2.evidence: plan :94116-94123 adds one test to packages/storage-browser/tests/phase-6a-creator-successor-product.pw.ts, which is test.describe.configure({ mode: "serial" }) at :662 with exactly three servers/pages and fixed DATABASES/CHANNEL_NAME (:41-42, :664-686) whose state the retained D.108d2/D.108e tests carry across titles.
p2.disposition: Pin the new realm explicitly in RED (fourth server/page or an added tests-only direct-room entry with distinct database and channel names) and assert in the same run that the three retained realms' snapshots and authority are unchanged.

p2.title: The "idempotent same-head activation" gate has exactly one genuine producer, unnamed by the plan
p2.evidence: activateCreatorSuccessorAdoption consumes a one-use capability (packages/node/src/creator-adoption-activate.ts:245-248), so a second same-head activation cannot come from replaying the published capability; the only non-synthetic producer is the retained one-call API returning a fresh capability for an already-published head at packages/node/src/creator-adoption-commit.ts:684 (terminal.kind === "active-new" -> success(...)).
p2.disposition: Name that producer in the Batch-1 GREEN matrix so the idempotence case is minted from authenticated durable state rather than by re-minting activation material in the fixture.

summary: The bounded audit is accurate at every cited line and the RED is executable and causal: after a genuine 1->2 close the current closure holds a v3-live-generation-2 projection, so packages/node/src/creator-adoption.ts:371-374 finds no candidate and verifyCreatorSuccessorAdoption returns exact chain-invalid at :766, ahead of the journal and snapshot owners; the browser observation is equally causal because the room never rebinds close (examples/v3-room/src/index.ts:2265-2287, :3502) and sealEpoch reaches a handle already at lifecycle successor-adopted (packages/node/src/creator-close.ts:469-476, :638-643). Deriving kind/epoch from authenticated trust is sufficient and byte-identical at epoch 0: openCreatorSuccessorTrust already enforces successor == current + 1 (packages/protocol-v3/src/creator-close.ts:619), v3-live.ts:1928 and :4598 are already epoch-relative, and the floor (examples/v3-room/src/index.ts:936-981) and bindCreatorLiveClose (packages/node/src/creator-close.ts:424-428) plus epoch-filtered evidence rows (packages/seal/src/creator.ts:438-452) make product rebinding to the existing singular stores feasible with no new store, method, wire field, threshold, or cold-reopen change. Three P1s block: the plan's post-consumption "retain the old owner and lock" is impossible because activateV3LivePlane retires the predecessor at v3-live.ts:7261 before terminalizeSource at :7383 and the failure paths tear down the shared topic/queue; the duplicate-adoption predicate as worded would refuse the legitimate 1->2 adoption because the floor only advances inside the adoption; and the compatibility boundary omits the two retained epoch-1 authority oracles whose cheapest accommodation silently weakens the retained D.108d2 gate.
